clue.text: Insect consuming marine mollusc once

indicators.note: an insect consuming something takes it inside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a fly is a common insect
an ormer is an abalone, an edible sea snail found off the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A bug that used to eat sea snails.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at some earlier time, in the past.

clue.text: Not tired by fellow student

parts.note: fresh means full of energy, not weary
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A new undergraduate full of energy beside another scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year at university, especially in America, is called this.

clue.text: Official uniform

definitions.meaning: in accordance with rules, properly sanctioned

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both properly sanctioned and even or consistent in pattern.

clue.text: Number heading off from summit

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is taken away

parts.note: a height is a summit, a high point

explanation.surface: A count of people setting off from the top of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, one more than seven.

clue.text: Head of policy?

parts.note: reads like a senior official setting rules, but a policy is a line taken, so whoever runs it is a boss in that sense

explanation.surface: A question about who leads a government strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor with direct responsibility for an employee is that person's immediate boss.

clue.text: Henry's stolen from body to get drink

indicators.note: something stolen from a thing is taken out of it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a chassis is the body or frame of a car
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry has been robbed of his body, and a drink follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is the unit of inductance, symbol H, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, the drink mixed into kir.

clue.text: Hormone I'd learn about in article

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone discovers something about a hormone from a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' mixes I'D LEARN into DRENALI, which 'in' puts inside AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone released under stress, the fight-or-flight chemical.

clue.text: Fund gained from increase in activity

indicators.note: in places one word within the other

parts.note: sport is a physical activity
up as a noun is a rise, an increase

explanation.surface: Money raised from a rise in exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something is to back or finance it.

clue.text: Melons rotten? That's serious

indicators.note: rotten fruit is spoiled and broken down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave reaction to finding the fruit has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and earnest.

clue.text: Taking part can be delightful

definitions.meaning: ... in an activity means joining or participating in it
an ... manner is charming and attractive

explanation.definitionFit: Participating in something and being charming are both senses of the same participle.

clue.text: Stay on the Spanish launch

parts.note: a stay is a support, a prop
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone stays on in Spain to start something.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to drive or hurl it forward.

clue.text: Short break taken by the northern composer

parts.note: hols is the short, colloquial form of holidays, a break
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t', as in t' mill

explanation.surface: A northern musician takes a quick holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire and Lancashire speech 'the' is clipped to t'; 'taken by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets.

clue.text: Note's brief and means to deceive

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale, with the 's added
to brief someone is to inform them

explanation.surface: A memo's summary is designed to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone false information is to mislead or deceive them.

clue.text: Anne is hour late going around island

indicators.note: going around suggests turning about, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Anne is running behind schedule as she tours an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' shuffles ANNE IS, H and LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helena is the South Atlantic island where Napoleon died in exile.

clue.text: A vital force in reorganising plant

indicators.note: reorganising tells us the letters of the words before it are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A life force at work in rearranging a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganising' shuffles the thirteen letters of A VITAL FORCE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The African violet, a saintpaulia, is a popular flowering houseplant.

clue.text: Verbally abuse club celebrities after all

indicators.note: after places the celebrities following the word all

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
names are famous people, as in big names

explanation.surface: Insult the famous members of a club, after all.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone names is to insult them.

clue.text: Stock charge, perhaps

parts.note: reads as a fee for shares, but stock is livestock and the charge is a headlong rush

explanation.surface: A fee for buying shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush of frightened cattle or horses is the classic example.

clue.text: Information age?

definitions.meaning: being enlightened means being informed, given knowledge
the Age of ... was the eighteenth-century period of reason

explanation.definitionFit: The word means instruction or insight, and also names the 18th-century intellectual era.

clue.text: Authorise English and Scandinavian language around Germany

indicators.note: around puts the language outside the letter for Germany

parts.note: Norse is the old language of Scandinavia
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Approving a language course covering Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or sanction officially.

clue.text: Leave to collect data which may be crucial

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: exit means leave, go out
gen is informal British for information

explanation.surface: Permission to gather information that might be vital.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'which may be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing, urgent, demanding immediate action.

clue.text: Revolting old hat?

parts.note: reads as a disgusting worn hat, but suggests a cap worn by a rebellious crowd, an old-fashioned piece of headwear

explanation.surface: A disgusting, worn-out item of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A frilled cotton cap worn indoors by women in the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: Dread one union leader becoming involved in battle

indicators.note: becoming involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are mixed
a union's leader is the first letter of the word union

explanation.surface: A trade-union boss's fears grow on getting drawn into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union leader' gives U, which 'becoming involved' mixes with DREAD and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oudenarde (1708) was a victory of Marlborough's in the War of the Spanish Succession.

clue.text: Quarter included in precise figure

indicators.note: one piece included in another is placed inside it

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and precise
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A fourth part fits within an exact number.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a solid geometric figure with two identical ends and flat sides.

clue.text: Player integral to group, I perceive

indicators.note: integral to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician seems essential to the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or a pipe, so is a musician.

clue.text: Check about having order for pigment

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: having means holding something within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a paint has been ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome yellow and chrome green are pigments made from chromium compounds.

clue.text: Hard work producing elaborate arrangement

parts.note: set means hardened, as concrete sets
a piece is a work, as of art or music

explanation.surface: Graft leading to a complicated plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A set piece is a carefully planned, formal display or routine.

clue.text: Satisfy requests, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is chosen for how it is pronounced

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests or appeals

explanation.surface: Someone tries to meet demands that sound reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone is to give them what they want, to satisfy them.

clue.text: Artist friend is full of tenacity

indicators.note: a thing that is full of something holds it inside

parts.note: mate is a friend
grit is courage and determination

explanation.surface: A determined pal who paints.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter.
